title: DWI Connectome-based Sex Classification in Young using Supervised Variational Autoencoder
abstract: arXiv:2610.16348v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: During adolescence, significant changes in brain development are influenced by hormonal changes that impact both the body and the brain. This study presents sex classification in 787 young adults having age range of 15-25 years using Diffusion-weighted (DWI) structural connectome, focusing on 82 Desikan-Killiany atlas ROIs. A supervised variational autoencoder (SVAE) is used to extract latent space features from DWI connectome data. Although several studies explored differences in brain structure and function between sexes, the main contribution of this study lies in incorporating SVAE to learn a compact, regularized latent representation for the task of sex classification. Initial exploratory data analysis shows that these features can capture the differences in sex-specific latent space patterns. translated_title: 基于DWI连接组和监督变分自编码器的年轻人性别分类
translated_abstract: 在青春期，大脑发育的重大变化受到激素变化的影响，这些激素变化同时作用于身体和大脑。本研究使用扩散加权（DWI）结构连接组，对787名年龄在15-25岁之间的年轻人进行性别分类，重点关注82个Desikan-Killiany图谱感兴趣区域（ROIs）。研究采用监督变分自编码器（SVAE）从DWI连接组数据中提取潜在空间特征。尽管已有多项研究探索了不同性别在大脑结构和功能上的差异，本研究的主要贡献在于将SVAE融入性别分类任务中，学习一种紧凑的、正则化的潜在表示。初步的探索性数据分析表明，这些特征能够捕捉性别特异性潜在空间模式的差异。随后，学习到的潜在空间SVAE特征被输入到不同的机器学习模型中进行性别分类。在所考虑的机器学习分类器中……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究的主要贡献在于将监督变分自编码器（SVAE）应用于DWI结构连接组数据，学习紧凑且正则化的潜在特征表示，实现了787名15-25岁年轻人的性别分类。
en_tdlr: The main contribution of this study is incorporating a supervised variational autoencoder (SVAE) to learn compact, regularized latent representations from DWI structural connectomes for sex classification of 787 young adults aged 15-25.
